purpose: Record what Yamada's 1967 Itbayat fishing-vocabulary article says about freshwater fish names, distinguish source labels from modern taxonomy and wild-occurrence claims, and retain the lead as research-only evidence.

source.title: Fishing Economy of the Itbayat, Batanes, Philippines with Special Reference to its Vocabulary
source.author: Yukihiro Yamada
source.publication: Asian Studies, 5(1), 1967; article begins on printed page 137; freshwater fish list on printed page 194
source.materialReviewed: Article context and printed page 194. No other issue items were used.
source.license: No item-specific open reuse license verified in reviewed issue metadata

contextAndMethod.geographicScope: Itbayat Island, Batanes, at island scale only; no named freshwater waterbody, station, or capture locality is supplied for the freshwater list.
contextAndMethod.sourceType: Ethnographic and linguistic description of Itbayat fishing life and vocabulary, not a standardized ichthyological survey.
contextAndMethod.fieldContext: The author says the paper draws on field visits to Batanes in June 1965 and May 1966, totaling one month, plus informant material gathered in Manila. The introduction credits ichthyologists with helping identify some fishes, but the freshwater list gives no specimen-level identification trail.
contextAndMethod.sourceStatement: The article introduces a short list as freshwater fishes and animals, then lists local/source names and brief glosses. It does not report sampling effort, dates per fish, vouchers, or waterbody-level observations.

sourceReportedFishLabels.sourceDescription: A species of fish called mudfish.
sourceReportedFishLabels.taxonomicDisposition: Unresolved common/local label. Do not infer Channa striata or another species from the English gloss alone.
sourceReportedFishLabels.evidenceClass: historical freshwater vocabulary label; no voucher or site-resolved capture record

sourceReportedFishLabels.sourceDescription: A species of fish described as introduced recently (relative to the article's 1960s context).
sourceReportedFishLabels.taxonomicDisposition: Unresolved to species; no exact introduction date, stock origin, capture record, or waterbody is given.
sourceReportedFishLabels.evidenceClass: historical introduction statement in an ethnographic vocabulary list; not proof of a current wild population or of Kayaywan/Kavaywan Lake stocking

sourceReportedFishLabels.sourceDescription: A big eel; the article prints Anguilla mauritiana Bennett and cross-references katuna as one sample/type of water eel.
sourceReportedFishLabels.taxonomicDisposition: Retain the article's name verbatim. Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes currently lists A. mauritiana as a synonym of Anguilla marmorata, while also documenting competing historical synonym treatments. This is a nomenclatural candidate only; it does not re-identify the source's eel without a specimen or diagnostic material.
sourceReportedFishLabels.evidenceClass: historical freshwater vocabulary and old scientific-name label; no voucher, dated capture, or named waterbody

relatedFreshwaterAnimals.scopeNote: The same list includes shrimp, a shell animal, and crab labels. They are not fish taxa and were not converted to species identities.

identityAndTaxonomyCrosswalk.authority: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, California Academy of Sciences; online version updated 13 August 2026
identityAndTaxonomyCrosswalk.currentCatalogDisposition: Synonym of Anguilla marmorata Quoy & Gaimard, 1824
identityAndTaxonomyCrosswalk.conflictAndLimit: The Catalog records prior synonym treatments under A. anguilla and A. bengalensis as well as A. marmorata and currently gives A. marmorata. The synonym record cannot establish the biological identity of Yamada's unvouchered local-name entry.

waterbodyNameCrosswalk.reason: The article does not identify a particular lake, river, stream, spring, or capture site; no crosswaterbody inference is justified.

qualityAndReuseLimits: This 1967 ethnographic and vocabulary article is historical cultural evidence, not a contemporary fish inventory, standardized survey, or abundance estimate.
The freshwater labels have no species-by-waterbody, capture date, method, voucher, accession, or coordinates; no occurrence, geometry, present-day range, or map pin is derived.
Dalag and tilapia remain unresolved source labels; the historical introduction note does not identify a species or prove present wild status.
The Anguilla synonym crosswalk concerns nomenclature only and does not independently identify an unvouchered Itbayat eel.
Do not derive diet, bait, catchability, safety, legal access, conservation status, or present-day abundance from this source.
No item-specific open reuse license was verified. Only concise attributed factual notes are retained; no article prose, image, figure, or table is reproduced. Publication approval remains false.

sources.supports: Historical Itbayat freshwater vocabulary labels dalag, tilapia, and tuna; p. 194. The paper does not identify waterbodies or provide vouchers or a standardized fish survey.
Current Catalog of Fishes nomenclatural treatment of Anguilla mauritiana as a synonym of A. marmorata, alongside historical competing synonym treatments.
Separate recent Itbayat fish-cage context naming Kavaywan Lake, Raele on page 9; the ethnographic labels are not linked to this lake.
